title: Pass a drill by its body in both hands, handle into a coworker's palm
instruction: Your coworker holds out their right hand, palm up, for the drill. Holding it by its body with both hands, never by the handle, lay the handle across their palm with the chuck pointing out along their fingers, never at them. Move slowly near their hand without bumping it, and let go once the drill rests in it.
context: Passing power tools is routine on job sites: handle first, directly to the worker, pointed away from people (CCOHS hand tools; OSHA 3080). Unlike a knife or scissors, a pistol drill's pose has two axes: its grip must lie across the palm, housing over the thumb, chuck out along the fingers, so the hand closes on a working grip. Its balance point is inside the grip, which must stay free for the receiver (Cini et al., Sci. Robot. 2019), so a gripper can only hold the body, off balance: one parallel-jaw grip lets the 0.9 kg drill twist. Two grips straddling the centre of mass hold it level, but form a closed chain: the arms must lift, turn and lower it as one rigid body. It must move under 0.25 m/s near the hand (OSHA's reduced robot speed) and be let go only once it rests (Chan et al., HRI 2012). Two hands are for control with grippers; no safety rule asks people to pass a drill two-handed.
setup: Dream Labs' YAM station (scene=station), both arms at their ready pose. World frame: origin between the arm bases, x forward (away from the robot), y to the left, z up; the table top is at z = 0.7475 m. The drill is Arena's library asset cordless_drill_ycb_robolab (the YCB power-drill scan: plastic body, metal chuck) at full size (18.4 x 18.7 x 5.7 cm), its mass set to 0.895 kg (the YCB power drill's), lying on its side centred at x 0.2 m, y -0.175 m, turned 45 degrees from how it goes on the hand: its chuck points back toward the robot's right arm (-x, -y) and its battery away from the robot and to the right (+x, -y). The coworker's right hand, glove cuff and sleeve are fixed boxes (hi-vis yellow work glove, sRGB 0.85, 0.90, 0.15; navy sleeve, sRGB 0.10, 0.14, 0.30), held palm up with the fingers toward the robot: the palm is 10 x 9 x 4 cm, its top 4 cm above the table, centred at x 0.36 m, y 0.03 m; four fingers, each 2 cm wide, 1.8 cm thick and 6.6 to 8.8 cm long, run toward the robot from the knuckle line at x 0.31 m, their tops 4 mm below the palm's, so they float 1.8 cm above the table; the thumb (9.5 x 3.2 x 2.2 cm) lies along x at y 0.149 m, centred at x 0.3475 m, its top level with the palm's, joined to the palm by a 4 x 5.8 cm web 1.5 cm thick (1.0 to 2.5 cm above the table, centred at x 0.39 m, y 0.104 m); the cuff (x 0.41 to 0.45 m) is 7 cm wide and 3.6 cm tall and the sleeve (x 0.45 to 0.91 m) 8 cm wide and 6.5 cm tall, both lying along the table at y 0.03 m, toward the coworker, who stands across the table at x 1.08 m, y -0.17 m. Handed over correctly, the middle of the drill's handle is over x 0.36 m, y 0.065 m, the battery rests on the palm and the motor housing on the thumb. The drill starts 11 cm from that point, inside the 15 cm slow zone, so the speed limit applies throughout. All objects share one rubber-like friction (static 1.2, dynamic 1.0). The layout is fixed (-E object_jitter=0).
scoring: The score is a ladder read at the end of the trial. 0.25: the drill was lifted (its lowest point 2 cm or more above the table) and afterwards its bounding box came within 7 cm of the palm point (x 0.36 m, y 0.065 m, at the palm's top). 0.5: it now also rests on the hand: settled (at rest, under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s, in at least 3 of the last 5 control steps), lying flat within 10 degrees, the lowest corner of its bounding box within 1 cm of the palm top, and the middle of its handle within 6 cm (horizontally) of the palm point. 0.75: also handle first: the middle of the handle within 2 cm of the palm point, the handle running across the palm toward the thumb (+y, battery to motor housing) and the chuck pointing out along the fingers (-x), each within 20 degrees. 1.0: also handed over: both grippers' TCPs at least 7 cm from the drill's bounding box. A full score counts once it has held for 1 s (until then it reads 0.75), and holding it for 1 s ends the trial as a success. Caps, kept for the rest of the trial: the chuck pointing within 30 degrees of the direction from its tip to any point of the coworker's body (a vertical line at x 1.08 m, y -0.17 m, from the floor to 1.75 m) for 2 control steps in a row while the drill is lifted caps the score at 0.25; any point of the drill moving faster than 0.25 m/s (its centre's speed plus its spin times 15.5 cm, the farthest any point of it is from its centre of mass) for 2 control steps in a row while its bounding box is within 15 cm of the palm point caps it at 0.5; carrying it (moving it, or holding it up off the table and the hand) with a gripper closed on it whose pads' centre line (from the TCP to the pad tips, 13 mm past the TCP) passes within 5 mm of the handle's box caps it at 0.5; carrying it in the air (its lowest point 5 mm or more above the table and not down on the hand, i.e. not with its lowest corner within 1 cm of the palm top and the middle of its handle within 6 cm of the palm point) held by fewer than both grippers for 10 control steps in all (0.5 s at 20 Hz, over the whole trial) caps it at 0.5, so it must be carried with both hands, while the grippers may close on it one at a time on the table and let go one at a time once it lies on the hand (lying still with no gripper on it, it is not being carried); any part of the drill (motor housing, handle or battery, each as a box) overlapping the coworker's glove cuff or sleeve caps it at 0.5; a TCP or any point of the finger pads (27 mm wide, from their tips up 30 mm) coming within 3 mm of the coworker's hand, cuff or sleeve caps it at 0.5. A drop scores 0: the drill falls 2 cm or more below where it was last held or at rest while no gripper holds it. A gripper holds it when its TCP is within 1 cm of the drill's own bounding box (in the drill's frame, turned with it), its fingers are 2.5 to 8.5 cm apart, and the drill moved with it since the previous control step (the point of the drill where the TCP was is still within 5 mm of it). The TCPs and pads come from the arms' joint positions through the framework's forward kinematics; if they can't be read, the score is capped at 0.75. On real arms: grips, speed, aim and contact from 20 fps video; the end pose from a top photo and a tape.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed: every trial starts with the drill at its start pose and the coworker's hand empty.
fidelity: The hand is fixed boxes that never grasp or move, so handed over means at rest on the open palm. The drill is Arena's YCB scan, one rigid body (no trigger, chuck or battery release), mass set to YCB's 895 g. Holding and contact are judged from TCP pose, finger pads and opening, and the drill moving with the gripper: no contact sensors. Friction 1.2/1.0, grippier than a glove. The task file redirects Arena 0.3.1's dead staging URL for the drill to NVIDIA's production copy.
